prompt: In cleanroom operation, what is the most important source of contamination to control?
correct: Particles generated by people
explanation: That is why gowning, slow movement and personal cleanliness matter so much.
quote: particles generated by people are the most important concern in the cleanroom operation

prompt: Which of these is NOT allowed when you go into a cleanroom?
correct: Wearing makeup, perfume or cologne
explanation: Cosmetics and scented products shed particles and chemicals.
quote: Wear cosmetics, perfume, cologne, or other similar scented products.

prompt: How should you move inside a cleanroom?
correct: Slowly, without running or unnecessary movement, to minimize air disturbance
options: Slowly, without running or unnecessary movement, to minimize air disturbance
Quickly, to spend less time inside
Jogging is fine if you are gowned
However you like; airflow handles it
explanation: Fast movement stirs up particles.
quote: Walk rapidly, jog/run, or move unnecessarily (try to minimize air disturbance).

prompt: What can you write with inside a cleanroom?
correct: Cleanroom-approved paper and notebooks with a ball-point pen
options: Cleanroom-approved paper and notebooks with a ball-point pen
A pencil on ordinary printer paper
explanation: Pencils, regular paper and impact printers are not allowed.
quote: Use cleanroom approved paper, notebooks, ball-point pens, and tape.

prompt: Which of these may NOT be brought into a cleanroom?
correct: Regular paper, cardboard, bubble wrap or paper towels
options: Regular paper, cardboard, bubble wrap or paper towels
Items wiped down and approved for entry
explanation: Delivery packaging stays outside; check what your site allows before bringing anything in.
quote: Bring in regular paper, cardboard, Styrofoam, bubble wrap, paper towels, or scotch tape in cleanroom.

prompt: Can you chew gum or drink inside the cleanroom?
correct: No: no edibles, drinks or tobacco in cleanroom or clean areas
options: No: no edibles, drinks or tobacco in cleanroom or clean areas
Yes, if you stay near the door
explanation: Drink water before you go in.
quote: Consume edibles (mints, gums, candies, etc.), drinks, or use tobacco or similar products in cleanroom or clean areas.

prompt: An approved tool has to go into the cleanroom. What happens first?
correct: It is wiped down with 10% IPA / 90% DI water, using gloves and safety glasses
options: It is wiped down with 10% IPA / 90% DI water, using gloves and safety glasses
It is blown off with your breath
explanation: Nothing goes in without approval and wipe-down.
quote: Ensure that approved items are wiped down prior to entry with a solution of 10% IPA and 90% DI H2O, using gloves and safety glasses.

prompt: What footwear is not allowed in gowning areas or cleanrooms?
correct: Open-toe footwear such as sandals or flip-flops
options: Open-toe footwear such as sandals or flip-flops
explanation: Wear full shoes and long pants.
quote: No open-toe footwear is allowed in gowning areas or cleanrooms

prompt: How should a hairnet be worn when gowning?
correct: Containing all hair and covering the ears
options: Containing all hair and covering the ears
Over the top of the head only
Only if your hair is long
explanation: Hair must be fully covered.
quote: Put on hairnet. Contain all hair and cover ears.

prompt: You have a beard and you are wearing a cleanroom face mask. Do you still need a beard cover?
correct: Yes, a beard cover is still required
options: Yes, a beard cover is still required
Only if the beard is long
explanation: The beard cover must cover the facemask at all times.
quote: Beard covers are still required for personnel with facial hair when entering the cleanroom even while wearing your cleanroom mask.

prompt: What must you avoid while putting on cleanroom garments?
correct: Letting the garments touch the floor
options: Letting the garments touch the floor
explanation: The floor of the gowning room is the dirtiest surface you will touch.
quote: Do not allow garments to touch the floor during gowning.

prompt: Inside the cleanroom, what should you never do with your gloved hands?
correct: Touch your face
explanation: Keep hands, face and hair clean; the face sheds particles onto the glove.
quote: Keep personally clean - particularly hands, face, and hair; do not touch face with gloves.

prompt: How do you enter a cleanroom area?
correct: Only through the authorized gowning areas
options: Only through the authorized gowning areas
explanation: Follow the posted entry and exit flow.
quote: Entry to the cleanroom areas is through the authorized gowning areas only.

prompt: What is the first step of the gowning sequence in the sample cleanroom protocol?
correct: Clean street shoes in the shoe brush vacuum
options: Clean street shoes in the shoe brush vacuum
explanation: Then the tacky mat, sanitizer and gloves, hairnet, beard cover, shoe covers, and the rest top-down.
quote: Clean off street shoes in the shoe brush vacuum to remove large particles.

prompt: When must steel-toed safety shoes be worn in the sample cleanroom protocol?
correct: When handling heavy (over 30 lb) equipment, parts or assemblies
options: When handling heavy (over 30 lb) equipment, parts or assemblies
explanation: Cleanroom rules do not cancel ordinary safety rules.
quote: For any person handling heavy (>30 lbs.) equipment, parts or assemblies, steel-toed safety shoes are to be worn in the cleanroom areas.

prompt: According to OSHA, what share of heat-related deaths happen during a worker's first week on the job?
correct: Over 70 percent
options: None: heat deaths only happen after years
explanation: New workers are not yet acclimatized.
quote: Over 70 percent of heat-related deaths occur during a worker's first week

prompt: When do almost half of heat-related deaths occur?
correct: On a worker's first day on the job, or first day back after a long absence
options: On a worker's first day on the job, or first day back after a long absence
On the last day of the project
Only in the tenth year of work
explanation: Build heat tolerance gradually.
quote: Almost half of heat-related deaths occur on a worker's first day on the job

prompt: Under the OSHA/NIOSH 'Rule of 20 percent', how much should a new worker work in the heat on the first day?
correct: Only 20 percent of the normal duration
options: Only 20 percent of the normal duration
A full shift with no breaks
explanation: Duration is increased step by step over the following days.
quote: New workers should work only 20 percent of the normal duration on their first day.

prompt: How long should increased heat precautions last for new workers?
correct: 1 to 2 weeks
explanation: New workers should be monitored closely for heat illness symptoms.
quote: These increased precautions should last for 1-2 weeks.

prompt: You start a job in January. Can you lose heat acclimatization over the winter?
correct: Yes: workers can lose acclimatization during the cooler winter months
options: Yes: workers can lose acclimatization during the cooler winter months
Only if you move to a different country
explanation: Build the water habit early and re-acclimatize before the first hot season.
quote: They can also lose heat acclimatization during the winter, when temperatures are cooler.

prompt: When should workers drink water while working in the heat?
correct: Frequently, not just when they are thirsty
options: Frequently, not just when they are thirsty
explanation: Water should be cool, nearby, easy to get and sufficient for the whole shift.
quote: Workers should be encouraged to drink water frequently while working in the heat not just if they are thirsty.

prompt: A worker in the heat is confused and slurring their speech. What do you do?
correct: Treat it as heat stroke: cool them immediately and call 911
options: Treat it as heat stroke: cool them immediately and call 911
Tell them to finish the task and rest later
Wait an hour to see if it passes
explanation: Heat stroke is the most severe heat illness and needs immediate medical attention.
quote: Cool these workers immediately and call 911!

prompt: Which of these is a symptom of heat stroke?
correct: Confusion, disorientation, slurred speech or unconsciousness
options: Confusion, disorientation, slurred speech or unconsciousness
explanation: Mental dysfunction is the warning sign that separates heat stroke from milder heat illness.
quote: Workers suffering from heat stroke experience mental dysfunction such as unconsciousness, confusion, disorientation, or slurred speech.

prompt: Which is an occupational risk factor for heat illness that applies to full cleanroom garments?
correct: Wearing clothing that holds in body heat
options: Wearing clothing that holds in body heat
explanation: Other risk factors are heavy activity, hot conditions and lack of acclimatization.
quote: wearing clothing that holds in body heat

prompt: Can water alone replace the electrolytes lost by sweating over a long hot shift?
correct: No: other types of beverages are needed for electrolytes
options: No: other types of beverages are needed for electrolytes
explanation: For short jobs cool water is enough; long sweaty work needs electrolyte replacement too.
quote: Water cannot replace electrolytes; other types of beverages are needed.

prompt: What do students receive at the end of an OSHA Outreach 10-hour or 30-hour class?
correct: A course completion card
explanation: Keep the card for site entry; replacements go through the original trainer or online provider.
quote: Students receive an OSHA 10-hour or 30-hour course completion card at the end of the training.

prompt: Does an OSHA Outreach (10- or 30-hour) card meet the training requirements of OSHA standards?
correct: No: it is a voluntary program and does not meet the training requirements for any OSHA standard
options: No: it is a voluntary program and does not meet the training requirements for any OSHA standard
Yes, it covers every OSHA training requirement
explanation: Site-specific and task-specific training (LOTO, lifts, NFPA 70E) is still needed.
quote: this is a voluntary program and does not meet the training requirements for any OSHA standards

prompt: Who is the OSHA Outreach 30-hour class more appropriate for than the 10-hour class?
correct: Supervisors or workers with some safety responsibility
options: Supervisors or workers with some safety responsibility
explanation: The 10-hour class gives workers awareness of common job hazards.
quote: the 30-hour class is more appropriate for supervisors or workers with some safety responsibility

prompt: Can a replacement OSHA Outreach card be issued for a class completed more than 5 years ago?
correct: No: cards cannot be issued if the class was completed 5 years ago
options: No: cards cannot be issued if the class was completed 5 years ago
Yes, at any time from OSHA directly
Yes, from the project's general contractor
explanation: Keep the original card safe and photographed.
quote: Cards cannot be issued if completed 5 years ago.
